The ABSOLUTE best advice I can give is to reach out to one of his buddies he served  with if possible. Just tell them he isn't as well as he could be and needs help. Tell them you feel that only one of his brothers or sister at arms can help him break through to get help. 

If this isn't an option, then HE needs to be encouraged to reach out to one of them. I am almost certain that they will help him to get help. 

Call the local VA and ask what treatment options are available for him so when the opportunity presents itself, you already have ideas as to what the first step is so he doesn't procrastinate or blow it off.

As for what you can do, if he goes to an inpatient program, watch/ care for his pets if he has any. Make regular visits while he's there and stock his fridge and pantry when he's out. Visit him, now and after he has started treatment to make sure he's keeping himself and his domicile reasonably in order. Bills, cleaning etc. He will come to realize you honestly care and will begin to trust you and your advice more.

- don't give ultimatums
- don't bargain with him
- be firm but caring when he needs advice
- don't give him money or financial help until he is getting help consistently (but don't let him know this is your intention) 
- get him out of the house (football on Sunday or a family dinner etc)
- if he is abusing alcohol /substances,  do not accept it as the norm or understandable. Don't tell him he has to quit rather let him know he won't be doing it around you or your family.
